title: Creality Ender-3 1.1.x Melzi (ATmega1284P)
description: Original Ender-3 / CR-10 Melzi-style boards with an ATmega1284P at 16 MHz, serial at 250000 baud over a CH340, flashed with avrdude through the Optiboot-style bootloader.
dda_note: ATmega1284P at 16 MHz. 8 kHz DDA = 2000 clock ticks per tick; max 4,000 steps/s per axis, i.e. 50 mm/s at 80 steps/mm. Conservative; ISR cost not measured.
serial_usb: CH340 USB-serial as /dev/ttyUSB0, 250000 baud after Klipper is running.
notes: Compile-only: built in a sandbox with Klipper v0.13.0; never flashed or run on this board by the author.

Flashing baud 57600 comes from the comment in Klipper's config/printer-creality-ender3-2018.cfg ('avrdude -p atmega1284p -c arduino -b 57600 -P /dev/ttyUSB0 -U out/klipper.elf.hex'). Boards without a bootloader need an ISP programmer and are NOT covered.
UNVERIFIED: many Melzi clones ship without a bootloader or with a different baud; if flashing fails, see Klipper docs/Bootloaders.md.
UNVERIFIED: 1284P has 16 KiB RAM and 128 KiB flash; check the size numbers before enabling more features.

build_sizes.note: Klipper v0.13.0, arm-none-eabi/avr gcc from Ubuntu apt, sandbox build. RAM = static data+bss only; the segment queue itself is allocated at run time (depth * sizeof(segment): 24 bytes ARM, 23 bytes AVR).

sources: Klipper v0.13.0 config/printer-creality-ender3-2018.cfg and config/generic-melzi.cfg (header comments)
